title: The Well-Keeper
text: An old woman sits knitting by a well, a bucket of gold at her feet catching the light. A drink, she says, costs a true answer to one question. She does not look up from her knitting; she already knows the question.

options.label: The Leader drinks and answers truly, whatever she asks.

outcomes.text: She asks something hard. The truth costs them, but the water heals.

options.label: The best liar drinks and lies, hoping she does not notice.

outcomes.text: She laughs and lets it pass.
The water turns to sand in their mouth. Their tongue stays dry a long while.

options.label: Go thirsty; some questions cost more than water is worth.

outcomes.text: You leave thirsty and none the wiser. She never once looks up.
